title: decompose-ci-cache-keys-and-standardize-release-artifact-names
author: Anika Sharma
release_notes: Small CI and release pipeline refactor: split cache keying per toolchain, shorten and standardize release artifact names, add migration script for existing caches, update docs and examples.
description: Context and motivation: our CI cache key strategy conflates multiple dimensions (OS, toolchain, python/ts version, build profile) into a single long key which has caused inefficient cache misses and made targeted eviction impossible. Release artifact names are similarly ad-hoc (mix of timestamps, branch names, and UUIDs), making rollbacks and S3 lifecycle rules brittle. This PR does two coordinated things: (1) decompose cache keys into orthogonal namespaces so runners only invalidate the subset they depend on; (2) standardize release artifact naming to a compact, parseable schema and add a compatibility layer for older artifact names. Summary of changes: - Introduce per-layer cache keys: toolchain-, deps-, build-output-, and test-cache namespaces. - Implement helper library scripts/.github/actions/cache-key-utils to compute composed keys and backwards-compatible lookups. - Change release pipeline to emit artifacts with names like redwood-{repo}-{ref}-{sha-short}-{platform}.{ext} and attach metadata file {artifact}.meta.json for provenance. - Add migration script ci/migrate_caches.py to map old cache entries to new namespaces for the last 30 days. - Update docs: docs/ci/cache.md and docs/release/artifacts.md with examples and operational runbooks. - Add unit tests for key generation and integration test that uploads a dummy artifact and verifies naming + metadata. Checklist: - [x] Design review with infra/sre (ENG-3126) - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Docs updated - [x] Migration script added - [x] Verified in ephemeral runner on staging (see CI logs) Commits (high level): - feat(ci): decompose cache key generator and add per-namespace keys - chore(ci): introduce cache-key-utils action and helper script - feat(release): normalize artifact name and attach .meta.json files - chore(misc): docs for cache and release naming, tests, migration script Notes on implementation: cache keys are now represented as short hashed tokens per namespace (e.g. deps:depsha-7f3c, toolchain:tc-2026-02). The composite lookup in restore step tries to fetch in order of most-specific to least-specific so smaller changes won't invalidate larger caches unnecessarily. The migration script uses the GitHub Actions cache API with a best-effort remap for entries created in the last 30 days; older entries are left untouched to avoid spurious API rates. Files/areas changed (high level): - .github/workflows/ci.yml (split cache steps, new restore order) - .github/actions/cache-key-utils/* (new action) - ci/cache_utils.py, ci/migrate_caches.py (migration + helpers) - ci/tests/test_cache_key_generation.py (unit tests) - release/publish.yml (artifact naming + metadata upload) - docs/ci/cache.md, docs/release/artifacts.md - small adjustments in scripts that publish darwin/linux wheels and docker tags Review conversation (selected threads): - Diego Alvarez (2026-02-19): "Can we keep the legacy key lookup for at least 2 weeks and also log metrics on misses so SRE can observe impact?" -> Author: "Yes — added legacy lookup path in restore step and emit a short metric to the actions output. Migration script will also emit a mapping CSV that we can ingest into monitoring." - Maya Chen (2026-02-20): "Tests look good. Please ensure the composite lookup respects timeouts for remote cache APIs." -> Author: "Addressed: added 1s per-namespace client timeout and exponential backoff for retries." - Ravi Patel (2026-02-21): "Concern: artifact metadata contains branch name which can expose internal branches. Recommend switching to ref-short and include branch only for release workflows." -> Author: "Changed: metadata now records ref-short and full branch is only included if the run has release:true flag. Updated docs to call out privacy considerations." - Diego Alvarez (final approval, 2026-02-22): "Approving — ran staging workflow, cache hit rate improved and artifact naming looks clean." CI summary: - Main (matrix linux/darwin/windows, python 3.10/3.11, node 18): all checks passed after second run (one flaky test fixed by adding small timeout). - Integration: artifact publish workflow ran against staging bucket and produced expected artifact + .meta.json. - Lint: no new lint failures. - Security scan: flagged one transitive dev dependency; pinned and re-ran scan, cleared. Migration and rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind continue-on-failure feature flag for 48h to observe cache hit metrics. 2) Run migrate_caches.py as low-priority job to remap recent entries (ops runbook included in docs). 3) After 48h and verification, flip feature flag and promote commit to protected branch. Rollback path: revert to previous CI pipeline by switching workflows to the prior commit and clearing new caches for a clean state. Operational notes: - Metrics to watch: actions.cache.hit_rate (per-namespace), artifact.publish.latency, migration.map_success_rate. - Should avoid running full-scale migration more than once; script is idempotent for 30-day window. - We keep legacy lookup for two weeks and will retire it via follow-up ENG task. Related work and references: ENG-3126 designed cache decomposition; ENG-3140 tracked release artifact inconsistencies; SUP-842 customer support ticket reported a broken rollback due to ambiguous artifact names. Merge: squash-merged to main on 2026-02-23 by Anika Sharma.
